status: Human-required outcomes remain accepted; Codex-selected D1/D4/D6 v1 is frozen under explicit human authorization for Muse implementation on 2026-10-13. No implemented engine, API or target qualification is claimed.
human_suggestion: Use a visible marker such as $"prompt" because build-time code generation can cost money.
recommendation: Accepted static $"..." prompts on named/inline traits, named custom keyword definitions, named styles, component inline attachments and renderer-header views. Ordinary quoted strings remain values/metadata. $Name is a no-prompt named-style attachment. Definition/application contracts follow implementation-contract.md; no anonymous keyword definition or prompted keyword application.
lexical_form: A dollar sign immediately followed by a JSON double-quoted string; preserve the existing JSON escape and Unicode rules. $ "..." is invalid. No interpolation, runtime evaluation or message-variant suffix.
given_rule_scope: Given retains named and inline model/field trait prompts as distinct contribution/reuse forms. Named custom keywords define standalone declarations through keyword Name(signature) [agent=profile] $"prompt", with standalone Name key=value applications and named required compile-time arguments. Initial reference kinds model, field(target,type) and operation plus checked scalar/enum/array constants do not impose a capability ceiling: future kinds/producers require explicit compiler/canonical-owner integration. No anonymous keyword definition, prompted application, positional/default guessing, executable Given binding or built-in redefinition. Novel keyword behavior need not lower to existing Can expressions.
generation_and_cost: The literal marks a discoverable generation unit/intent, not an instruction to charge or invoke a coding tool whenever a build visits it.

Explicit preparation/refinement and fresh full manual retry may invoke the configured CLI/model with finite controls and truthful available usage/cost reporting. Retry covers all current prompts in normal active app/build selection, including successful styles, using current source and recipes; no per-prompt names or unit list required.
Ordinary build/check uses saved compatible files with zero AI calls. Missing/stale files diagnose and identify the unit; they do not silently generate.

Keep tracked editable files, selective direct refinement, participating leases and reset/cancel/failure preservation. Working output/direct edits survive until acceptance. The frozen implementation contract selects compatible-recipe whole-Then jobs and one complete full-retry acceptance set/run journal; scoped refinement remains available.
non_generation_contexts: Prompt literals are invalid as ordinary runtime string values, labels, descriptions, translation/message variants or arbitrary expressions or do bodies. Ordinary When scenarios/handlers use normal Can implementations and are not generation targets. Generated behavior requires its source-owned typed contract; a closed default/derive/check target set does not limit new Given keyword semantics. Dollar signs within ordinary strings/comments remain content. Custom keyword application statements cannot carry prompts; anonymous inline keyword definitions are excluded. Inline trait prompts remain accepted property/rule contribution forms.
verified_current_facts: Canonical lexer has no authored dollar punctuation. Today the prefix is rejected as E1007 followed by ordinary STRING token; no new lexer behavior is claimed.
Targeted examples/compiler-fixture authored .can scans found no dollar-sign use. Compiler-generated $cohort metadata is unrelated to authored prompt syntax.
Canonical grammar has static JSON strings and no source string interpolation; the proposal preserves that distinction.
implementation_scope: Accepted design and authoring illustrations only: no compiler/runtime support, provider invocation or new generation-control implementation is claimed. Ordinary saved builds retain zero AI calls.

page / $"A calm workspace that stacks on narrow screens."

accepted_style_contract: Top-level style Name $"prompt" defines reusable CSS without a visual body. Ordinary rendered components/pages/custom instances carry one $"prompt" or $Name suffix; nonvisual declarations and top-level anonymous scopes are excluded. Ordinary wrappers are superseded. Generated view renderer prompts stay in the view header, with one optional second $"prompt" or $Name suffix on that header for renderer-root styling and canonical controls as its only children; no inline, wrapper or leaf style statement exists. Compatible named uses share CSS without AI or copied outputs, with separate checked root/part instances; caller styling respects child-host/interior ownership.
scope_correction: Initial generation has three categories: Given extensions including traits and custom keywords, Then scoped styles and custom reusable Then rendering. The human removal of ordinary When generation supersedes prior do-prompt adoption; the mandatory marker and other accepted generation choices remain unchanged. Historical JEV requests/results remain historical and do not advise this new scope. Manual retry supersedes prior targeted failed-only retry: all current prompts in the active app/build scope are freshly regenerated. The frozen implementation contract selects compatible-recipe whole-Then jobs and one complete full-retry acceptance set/run journal; scoped refinement remains available.

generator_output_submission.status: Human-required custom MCP output-submission boundary accepted; generation engine/server/adapters unimplemented.
generator_output_submission.input: The host supplies captured generation context plus server-issued allowed logical output targets. These targets describe admitted artifacts, not filesystem paths chosen by the generator.
generator_output_submission.submission: Build-time generator agents submit structured CSS, JavaScript and other generated code/content to the custom MCP server against those allowed logical targets. They must not create their own output files or supply filesystem destinations.
generator_output_submission.host_ownership: The host validates each submission and controls correct placement, writing isolated candidate files and their provenance/required metadata. Existing validation, leases, current-input/byte/fence checks and acceptance controls govern promotion; submission alone does not accept output.
generator_output_submission.enforcement: Adapters must enforce a read-only/no-write generator environment for protected project, current-output and candidate-output files, with generic write tools and filesystem shell writes disabled for those locations. MCP alone does not isolate filesystem access, and a prompt-only promise is insufficient. Diagnose unsupported runner MCP or enforceable no-write capabilities before launching generation; do not fall back to direct generator file writes. Native CLI session/cache housekeeping may be separately isolated and is not generated application output.
generator_output_submission.lifetime: Private bounded Node tooling session; no new package or persistent daemon. Selected tools: generation_context for immutable context/handles/roles and generation_submit for batches of {target, role, content}; UTF-8 text and checked encoded assets. Transport remains adapter-specific and protected no-write enforcement gates launch.
generator_output_submission.job_grouping: Selected D6 v1: Given preparation precedes dependent frontend consumers; jobs group by compatible effective complete recipe and every frontend job receives whole-Then context plus all style/view intents/use contracts. All required full-retry outputs validate and accept together under one run journal. Incomplete/failed/conflicting sets preserve every current group; recovery restores the whole old set before commit or finishes the whole new set after commit. Selective refinement retains its declared scope. One CLI job may make many model/tool calls.
generator_output_submission.authoring_agent: The user-facing coding agent authoring .can remains permitted to inspect and directly edit primary generated files with existing participating edit leases. It is distinct from the launched build-time generator whose output must pass through MCP.
